idiom_name: struct with private(set) state and mutating methods (class for identity)
implementation_notes: Swift's structs and enums are full object types - stored properties plus methods - so the data+behaviour binding is native; value semantics removes defensive copying, private(set) hides mutation, and mutating methods make state changes visible in the signature. Entities that must be shared by reference (or need deinit or reference identity) are classes; value objects are structs or enums with validating (failable or throwing) initializers. Protocols provide the seam for repositories and services, keeping the model free of infrastructure.
pitfalls: Value semantics copy on assignment and parameter passing: add(_:) mutates a copy, so an entity that must be shared between screens should be a class (or live in an observable store).
private(set) still exposes the getter, so raw state escapes; expose derived queries when the internal representation should not be read directly.
Classes captured by escaping closures need [weak self] or they leak; structs avoid retain cycles but cannot provide identity.
